lesson.subject: science
lesson.title: Animals and Us
lesson.summary: Animal groups, our five senses, caring for our teeth and bodies, and how animals and people grow.
learning_objectives: Name the five senses and the body part for each
Say how to look after teeth and stay healthy
Put a life cycle in order

standards.text: Identify and name a variety of common animals including fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds and mammals
Identify, name, draw and label the basic parts of the human body and say which part is associated with each sense
Describe the importance for humans of exercise, eating the right amounts of different types of food, and hygiene

success_criteria: I can say which group an animal belongs to
I can name the five senses
I can say how to keep my teeth and body healthy
I can put a life cycle in order
lesson.real_life: Brushing your teeth, washing your hands and noticing animals at the park.

warm_up.prompt: Which of these is a living thing?
warm_up.explanation: A cat is alive. A chair and a spoon never were.

blocks.markdown:
Today's big question: how are animals and people alike?

We will find out about groups, senses and growing up.
blocks.say: Welcome back, young scientist! Today's big question is: how are animals and people the same, and how are they different? By the end, you will sort animals into groups, use your five senses, look after your body and teeth, and see how animals grow. Let's go!

blocks.alt: Animals and people have a lot in common.
blocks.caption: Animals and people have a lot in common.

terms.meaning: Living things that move, eat and have babies.

blocks.markdown:
**Mammals** have fur or hair and feed their babies milk.

**Birds** have feathers and lay eggs.

**Fish** have scales and fins.
blocks.say: Scientists put animals into groups by looking at how they are alike. Mammals have fur or hair, and the babies drink milk. A cat, a goat and you are mammals! Birds have feathers and wings, and they lay eggs. Fish have scales and fins, and they live in water. Let's meet each group.

scenes.caption: Mammals: goat, cat and cow.
scenes.say: Mammals have hair or fur. Goats, cats and cows are mammals. Their babies drink milk from their mothers.

scenes.caption: Birds: sparrow, parrot and hen.
scenes.say: Birds have feathers and wings. A sparrow and a parrot are birds. Most birds can fly, and every bird lays eggs.

scenes.caption: Fish live in water.
scenes.say: Fish live in water. They have scales and fins, and they breathe with gills.

question.explanation: Birds are the animals with feathers.

blocks.markdown:
**Reptiles** have dry, scaly skin.

**Amphibians** have wet skin and start life in water.
blocks.say: Two more groups. Reptiles have dry skin covered in scales. Snakes, lizards and crocodiles are reptiles. Amphibians, like frogs, start life in water and have wet, smooth skin. Look at one animal from each group.

blocks.alt: Reptiles: a snake, a lizard and a crocodile.
blocks.caption: Reptiles: a snake, a lizard and a crocodile.

question.prompt: A frog starts life in water and has wet skin. What group is a frog in?

points: Mammals have fur or hair and feed their babies milk
Birds have feathers and lay eggs
Reptiles have dry scales; amphibians start in water
blocks.say: Let us remember. Mammals have fur and milk. Birds have feathers. Fish have scales and fins. Reptiles have dry scales. Amphibians start in water.

terms.meaning: Animals with fur or hair that feed their babies milk.
Animals with feathers and wings that lay eggs.
Animals with scales and fins that live in water.
Animals with dry, scaly skin, like snakes and lizards.
Animals with wet skin that start life in water, like frogs.

blocks.markdown:
We have five **senses**: sight, hearing, smell, taste and touch.

Each sense uses a part of the body.
blocks.say: You find out about the world with your five senses. Your eyes see. Your ears hear. Your nose smells. Your tongue tastes. And your skin feels things like soft, rough, hot and cold. Look at all five.

scenes.caption: Sight: eyes.
scenes.say: Your eyes help you see colours, shapes and your family.

scenes.caption: Hearing: ears.
scenes.say: Your ears help you hear voices, birds and the call to prayer.

scenes.caption: Smell: nose.
scenes.say: Your nose helps you smell rice cooking.

scenes.caption: Taste: tongue.
scenes.say: Your tongue helps you taste sweet mangoes and sour lemons.

scenes.caption: Touch: skin.
scenes.say: Your skin helps you feel soft, rough, hot and cold things.

question.prompt: Which part of your body helps you hear?
question.hint: Which part is on the side of your head?

blocks.title: Which sense?
blocks.goal: Sort the things. Put things you see in See. Put things you smell in Smell.
blocks.say: Time to use your senses! Put each thing in the right box. Does it use your eyes to see, or your nose to smell? Then try the senses walk with a grown-up.

points: We have five senses: sight, hearing, smell, taste and touch
Eyes see, ears hear, nose smells, tongue tastes, skin feels
blocks.say: Remember. We have five senses and each one uses a body part.

terms.meaning: The five ways we find out about the world: sight, hearing, smell, taste and touch.

blocks.markdown:
**Teeth** help us bite and chew food.

Brush twice a day, eat fewer sweets and visit the dentist.
blocks.say: We use our teeth to bite and chew. Our first teeth are milk teeth. They wobble and fall out when we are about six or seven, and bigger teeth grow in their place. Those grown-up teeth must last all our lives, so we look after them. We brush twice a day, eat fewer sweets, and visit the dentist. Many Muslims also clean their teeth with a miswak, a small twig, following the Sunnah.

scenes.caption: Sugar can harm teeth.
scenes.say: A tooth with sugar on it can get a hole. The sugar is eaten by tiny germs, and they make acid.

scenes.caption: Brushing cleans teeth.
scenes.say: Brushing washes the sugar away. Now the tooth is clean and shiny.

question.prompt: How often should we brush our teeth?
question.explanation: We brush in the morning and at night.

blocks.title: Healthy or not?
blocks.goal: Put healthy things in Healthy. Put things we should have fewer of in Not often.
blocks.say: To stay healthy, a body needs good food, water, sleep, exercise and clean hands. Washing your hands with soap stops germs spreading. Muslims wash their hands and faces for wudu before prayer, so it is a good habit already. Play the memory game, then tell me which habit you do best.

blocks.title: Healthy lights
blocks.goal: Watch the order, then copy it.
blocks.say: Warm up your memory. Watch the healthy things light up, then copy the order.

question.prompt: Washing your hands with soap helps stop germs spreading.

points: Brush your teeth twice a day
Good food, water, sleep, exercise and clean hands keep us healthy
blocks.say: Remember. Look after your teeth. Eat well, sleep well, move, and wash your hands.

terms.meaning: The hard white parts in your mouth for biting and chewing.

mini_quiz.explanation: Sleep and exercise keep us strong.

blocks.markdown:
A **life cycle** shows how an animal grows and changes.

An egg hatches into a chick, and the chick grows into a hen.
blocks.say: All animals grow and change. This is called a life cycle. A hen lays an egg. A chick grows inside, and then it hatches. The chick grows into a hen, and the hen lays eggs. Let us watch the life cycle go round.

scenes.caption: A chick hatches.
scenes.say: The egg cracks, and a chick comes out. Cheep cheep!

scenes.caption: The chick grows.
scenes.say: The chick grows bigger and gets feathers.

scenes.caption: A hen.
scenes.say: In time it is a hen, and the hen can lay eggs of her own.

question.prompt: Put the chicken life cycle in order.
question.explanation: An egg hatches into a chick that grows into a hen.

blocks.alt: A baby, a child and a grown-up.
blocks.caption: A baby, a child and a grown-up.
blocks.say: You have a life cycle too. You were a baby, then a toddler, a child, and one day you will be a grown-up. Think about how you have changed since you were a baby. You are taller, you can run, you can read. Talk to a grown-up about your baby photos.

blocks.title: My growing up chart
materials: Baby photos if you have them
instructions: Draw yourself as a baby, as you are now, and as a grown-up.
Write one thing you could not do as a baby but can do now.
Show your chart to your family.

blocks.say: Remember. Animals have life cycles. A chicken goes from egg to chick to hen. Humans grow and change too.
